claude.sample_unit: informed consent documents (each in 3 versions, rated by 4 surgeons and 4 laypersons)

links.outcome: Content quality (risk, overall) of LLM-simplified consent forms with vs without clinician revision
links.effect: Clinician revision raised risk score from 3.28 to 3.69 (p=0.016) and overall from 2.86 to 3.64 (p=0.004); LMM risk β=0.42, overall β=0.78; restored to original-level quality.
links.quote: The risk score increased from 3.28 (SD = 0.55) to 3.69 (SD = 0.66), p = 0.016; the overall score also rose from 2.86 (SD = 0.36) to 3.64 (SD = 0.31), p = 0.004.

links.outcome: Whether clinician verification/correction of LLM consent text restores omitted risk information
links.effect: LLM version lost risk content (3.61 to 3.28, p=0.016); clinician revision restored it (3.69), with no significant difference from original (p=0.558).
links.quote: LLMs improved readability and understanding, but risked omitting key medical information.

links.outcome: Layperson comprehension of LLM-simplified plain-language consent forms
links.effect: Comprehension rose from 2.64 (original) to 3.53 (LLM), p=0.008; LMM β=0.89, p<0.001; LLM+Clinician 3.81.
links.quote: In contrast, layperson comprehension improved significantly, with the average score increasing from 2.64 (SD = 0.57) to 3.53 (SD = 0.38), p = 0.008.

links.outcome: Completeness of risk content in LLM-generated simplified consent forms
links.effect: LLM risk score fell from 3.61 to 3.28 (p=0.016); overall from 3.53 to 2.86 (p=0.004); LMM risk β=-0.33, overall β=-0.67.
links.quote: We observed significant declines in content quality scores in the risk and overall dimensions, indicating that efforts to improve readability may lead to omissions or weakening of essential medical information 23 .

links.outcome: Output variability of LLM simplification across temperature settings
links.effect: Structural simplification consistent across web, 0.1 and 0.9 temperature; lower temperature retained more difficult terms, higher temperature gave more rephrasing and semantic variability.
links.quote: Lower-temperature outputs tended to retain more technical and difficult terminology, whereas higher-temperature outputs exhibited more extensive rephrasing and greater semantic variability.

unlisted_practices: LLM simplification of non-English (Chinese) surgical consent forms followed by clinician revision restoring risk content

openai.sample_unit: informed consent forms, with three versions each

links.effect: Average score increased from 2.64 (SD = 0.57) to 3.53 (SD = 0.38), p = 0.008.
links.quote: In contrast, layperson comprehension improved significantly, with the average score increasing from 2.64 (SD = 0.57) to 3.53 (SD = 0.38), p = 0.008.

links.effect: Lee-Yang index decreased from 28.04 (SD = 1.94) to 22.90 (SD = 1.86), p = 0.004.
links.quote: Compared with the original version, the LLM-simplified consent forms showed a significant decrease in the Lee-Yang readability index, from 28.04 (SD = 1.94) to 22.90 (SD = 1.86), p = 0.004.

links.effect: Risk score 3.28 to 3.69, p = 0.016; overall 2.86 to 3.64, p = 0.004.
links.quote: The risk score increased from 3.28 (SD = 0.55) to 3.69 (SD = 0.66), p = 0.016; the overall score also rose from 2.86 (SD = 0.36) to 3.64 (SD = 0.31), p = 0.004.

links.effect: Risk score decreased 3.61 to 3.28, p = 0.016; overall dropped 3.53 to 2.86, p = 0.004.
links.quote: Specifically, the risk score decreased from 3.61 (SD = 0.71) to 3.28 (SD = 0.55), p = 0.016, while the overall score dropped from 3.53 (SD = 0.29) to 2.86 (SD = 0.36), p = 0.004.

links.effect: Temperature 0.1 retained more technical terms; 0.9 showed more rephrasing and greater semantic variability.
links.quote: Lower-temperature outputs tended to retain more technical and difficult terminology, whereas higher-temperature outputs exhibited more extensive rephrasing and greater semantic variability.

links.outcome: Content quality scores for risk and overall impression
links.effect: Clinician revision increased content quality scores for risk from 3.28 (SD = 0.55) to 3.69 (SD = 0.66) (p = 0.016) and overall from 2.86 (SD = 0.36) to 3.64 (SD = 0.31) (p = 0.004) versus LLM alone.
links.quote: The risk score increased from 3.28 (SD = 0.55) to 3.69 (SD = 0.66), p = 0.016; the overall score also rose from 2.86 (SD = 0.36) to 3.64 (SD = 0.31), p = 0.004.
